newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish central bank chief sees higher deficits.
newsitem.headline: Turkish central bank chief sees higher deficits.

text.p: Turkish central bank governor Gazi Ercel said on Friday Turkey's current account and public deficits were expected to rise sharply this year.
"The current account deficit is estimated to rise to $6-$7 billion this year," Ercel told Reuters.
Turkey's current account deficit was $2.3 billion at end-1995.
Ercel said the public sector borrowing requirement (PSBR) was expected to reach nine to 10 percent of gross national product after 6.5 percent in 1995.
"However current account deficit is easily being financed by unregistered exports of some $5 to $10 billion," he said.
Ercel was referring to the so-called luggage trade mostly by East Europeans, Russians and Central Asians who come to Turkey as tourists but buy mainly Turkish textile products.
"Interest payments are widening the budget deficit," Ercel said, blaming high interest payments on domestic debts for the sharp rise.
He said the 1996 budget was likely to give a primary surplus -- the budget balance excluding debt interest payments -- of one two percent of the GNP.
